title: Prove the sharp 20-bit completed-error guard and gauge-invariant obstruction
body:
The complete PR5830 gauge word now has a **sharp 20-bit final-output guard** under an explicit completed-operation relative-error contract. A finite causal bound gives final error below0.978B at unit roundoff2^-20 and intermediate error below27B. With t additional bits, final error is below B*2^-t for every t>=0. Ideal field norm plus error stays below2^17 B; B is an initial field Hilbert-norm bound, not a dimension-free input-coordinate bit bound.

The new covariance theorem binds every actual operation to a normalized error timeline. All384 entry and399 exit conversions remain noisy identity sites. All395 omitted physical SCALEs remain exact normalized transitions. Deleting the virtual physical identities recovers the entire26,351-instruction word. The source's norm/cost optimization remains with its owner; no new gauge word is constructed here.

The direct uniform bound gives25 prefix/21 final guard bits; the normalized uniform bound gives26/23. The stronger causal calculation follows actual prior defects, retains signed cancellation, and uses checked upward rational-grid bounds without a global stability denominator. An exact admissible actual-input defect trace at19 bits gives error>1.79B. A MOVE/ADD-only trace gives error>1.70B and survives every field-constant signed scalar gauge of the same word. Both pass at t=0 and t=32, with every local allowance, independent adjoint sum and literal physical transport checked. Thus20 is the least integer guard for this contract, and pure gauge changes cannot remove the19-bit obstruction. This is not a lower bound for a hardware rounding rule with stronger correlations.

Verification covers the782-column arbitrary-input endpoint, complete local invoice/frames/ownership, every normalized prefix score, all final signed error coefficients and witnesses, a separate physical transpose, an attaining literal fixture, eight rejection controls and36 independent exact rational causal cases. Registered Python3.12, committed bytes/modes, source-corruption and read-only Git-free optimized replay pass. Full-history preflight was not run in the shallow checkout; hosted CI and independent scientific acceptance remain pending.

COPY including its coefficient, INIT and CLEAR are exact premises here. Native maps and gauges are unitary before each completed defect. Physical rounded children, exact resets/COPY, final compiler and fixed tapes remain open. All five framework assumptions and selected kappa retain their status.

[Canonical claim and handoff](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/2750#discussioncomment-19209731). Source PR5830: `dd3ffe4c1b391b8d757969a9aa9b2f7c02a32117`. Credit PR5830/5824/5822/5812, PR5819/5826/5831, Adam Gall, ywz65, PR2878 and all retained P104 sources. Ali Romman with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance; Apache-2.0. The unchanged test-only PR5761 dependency `ba8a9e640e1983f3c29993fefa3f46e8ed03313a` retains original authorship and provenance.

SOURCES.json now binds the exact retained input copies in this PR history; retained_predecessors preserves every original head, path, blob and SHA256 plus the retained file/archive member. Original and retained bytes were checked equal. Metadata, committed bytes/modes and declared-pin ancestry checks pass. Source bytes, mathematical assertions and scientific receipts are unchanged. The full-history preflight remains unrun in this shallow checkout. Hosted replay is queued for the new head.
